conventions.convention: Entropy and normalized information use natural logarithms and nats; a binary code of k_n bits has rate k_n ln(2)/n.
One-letter surprisal is −ln p(a) on positive support and is assigned zero at zero-mass symbols. Block information and typical sets are defined only on positive support.
Typicality uses |I_n−H(p)| ≤ ε, with ε > 0 and n ≥ 1; zero-probability words are excluded.
The source coordinates start at index 1, share one probability space, and are mutually independent with a common finite-alphabet law.
Codes are deterministic total encoder and decoder maps, with integer k_n ≥ 0; achieving R means block error tends to zero and limsup R_n ≤ R.
The non-identically distributed example uses consistent finite product laws and explicitly defines concentration toward a constant under these varying laws; it assumes no infinite-product extension.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite-alphabet IID source, every n ≥ 1 and ε > 0 satisfy P(|I_n(X^n)−H(p)| ≥ ε) ≤ V(p)/(nε²). Consequently I_n(X^n) → H(p) in probability.
For a finite-alphabet IID source and ε > 0, with δ_n = P(X^n ∉ T_n(ε)), one has 0 ≤ δ_n ≤ V(p)/(nε²), |T_n(ε)| ≤ exp(n(H(p)+ε)), and |T_n(ε)| ≥ (1−δ_n)exp(n(H(p)−ε)). In particular δ_n → 0.
On A_+ define self-information as −ln p(a), assigning zero off support; define V(p) as the p-weighted squared deviation from H(p), and p^n(x^n) as the product of the coordinate probabilities.

For a law p on a finite nonempty alphabet, deterministic fixed-length binary codes exist with e_n ≤ V(p)/√n and R_n ≤ H(p)+n^(−1/4)+2 ln(2)/n. Every such code sequence with e_n → 0 satisfies liminf R_n ≥ H(p); if limsup R_n < H(p), then e_n → 1.

seams_checked.note: The actual imported interface is the natural-log/nats convention. The finite entropy formula agrees with the separately cited published finite-distribution definition. No stronger KL or conditional-information result is imported.

This is a background page prerequisite. The downstream page explicitly converts nats to bits by division by ln(2), defines general block laws separately, and proves its general AEP coding criterion locally rather than applying the IID theorem to dependent sources.

The multisource definition treats each joint vector as one finite-alphabet IID letter. Joint typicality uses the supplied normalized information on positive support, and its probability lemma invokes exactly V(P)/(nε²) for that vector law.

The page declares this background prerequisite but contains no direct citation to a batch-9 item. Its prose retains finite alphabets and nats and attributes information-density concentration and resolvability to its own local suppliers.

The typical-projector lemma applies the AEP to the finite positive-eigenvalue law of a density operator, with natural-log entropy. Conditional non-identically distributed eigenvalue variables are handled separately by a variance calculation and Chebyshev, without extending the IID supplier.
